title: Reader UIAutomator helpers mis-tap non-clickable semantics nodes and leak chrome state
symptom: Reader interaction instrumentation tests passed individually but failed in mixed groups. Failures included TTS active playback not opening the settings sheet on the TTS tab, chapter navigation assertions missing the bottom chrome after a chapter step, and center-tap chrome tests seeing the bottom settings action without the expected top bar. Logcat showed UiObject2 clicking non-clickable Compose semantics nodes for actions such as Settings, TTS, and reading-mode pills.
root_cause: The shared UIAutomator helpers treated UiObject2.click() as a reliable action on Compose semantics nodes and returned success even when the node itself was not clickable. When chrome had auto-hidden, tapPrimaryAction fell through to slot coordinates without first re-revealing chrome. The reading-mode helpers also verified page/scroll mode by repeatedly toggling chrome, which could leave the next assertion in an intermediate chrome state.
fix: Add clickObjectCenter to click the visible bounds center of a UiObject2 and use it for reader UIAutomator actions instead of direct UiObject2.click().
Update tapPrimaryAction and tapChapterAction to reveal chrome with a center tap before coordinate fallback when the target action label is not currently visible.
Make ensureScrollMode and ensurePageMode single-purpose helpers: open settings, select the requested mode, close settings, then hide chrome if visible.
Add setUp and tearDown resetStoryAppState calls to ReaderAppearanceToggleTest and ReaderChromeTest so mixed reader interaction groups do not inherit reader settings or anchors.
Replace direct UiObject2.click() calls in reader interaction tests with clickObjectCenter for settings, TTS, chapter, theme, and book-card selections.
failed_attempts: Do not classify a mixed UIAutomator failure as a product bug until the failing test is rerun alone and the logcat/action path is inspected.
A visible single label such as Settings is not sufficient proof that the complete reader chrome is in the expected state; helpers that change modes should leave a known state for the caller.
Direct UiObject2.click() is unsafe for Compose semantics-only nodes; logcat may show a non-clickable node while the test helper still reports success.
impact: Reduces false-positive reader visual and interaction regressions and makes mixed emulator test groups a stronger signal for real UI bugs.
